topic: Fix the three-variable cyclic SEM X1=aX2+eps1, X2=bX1+cX3+eps2, X3=dX2+eps3 with abcd nonzero and 1-ab-cd nonzero. Disturbances are centered, non-Gaussian, have finite third moments, satisfy eps1 independent of eps3 and the path connected-set Markov plus Tramontano-Drton-Etesami independence-genericity conditions; eps2 may depend arbitrarily on both outer disturbances. The information input is the observed cumulant tensor through order K in {2,3}; the query is only (a,d). For candidate (alpha,delta), define residual cross-cumulants F11, F21 and F12. Construct the explicit observed-cumulant chart D and prove that D nonzero makes their complex common zero set the singleton (a,d), with a rational inverse from the linear first subresultant of two observable cubics. On a nonempty covariance-regular locus, construct a smooth one-dimensional legal order-two fiber for (a,d), proving the least identifying order is three; also prove the full observed law retains a two-dimensional (b,c) fiber. Estimate (a,d) by feasible overidentified GMM on a compact sixth-Wasserstein regular subclass with quantitative chart, Jacobian and influence-covariance margins, and derive a uniformly valid sandwich ellipse. Explicitly distinguish Draisma-Kuhnt-Zwiernik, Jiang, Mesters-Zwiernik, Ribot-Seigal-Zwiernik and the banked general cumulant-transfer obstruction. Consumer: a prospective BayCausal/WIHS extension may report outer coefficients as robust under an independently justified overlapping-cycle/path-dependence motif while leaving central coefficients as a sensitivity fiber; do not claim its published disjoint-cycle theorem already covers this motif. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The residual covariance equation eliminates delta as t(alpha)/l(alpha); substituting into F21 and F12 gives two observable cubics P and Q. On the nonzero chart, their first subresultant is linear, yielding a=-s0/s1 and d=t(a)/l(a). Exact expansion verifies the legal exponential-source witness, all chart factors, the singleton residual ideal, a rank-two Jacobian, 100 fresh rational perturbations, and a nonlinear-middle stress case. A five-source construction realizes every nearby positive-definite path covariance with independent non-Gaussian endpoints, producing a one-dimensional order-two query fiber; an explicit residual shear preserves a two-dimensional full-law central-coefficient fiber. Literature checks found no query-specific cyclic order-three inverse. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniform asymptotic linearity of feasible optimally weighted GMM on the stated compact sixth-moment class, including centered third-cumulant influence functions, covariance estimation, separation, and margin diagnostics. EARLY KILL TEST: Implement the fixed cubic subresultant using only observed tensors with the true mechanism hidden; reproduce both witness families and exact covariance twins on a rational neighborhood. Stop if a nontrue common root survives with D nonzero, specialization fails, or the covariance realization leaves the legal model. open_problems.why_unsolved: Tramontano–Drton–Etesami obtain a complete direct-effect criterion only in the acyclic case and partial results for cycles; their full-distribution transformation argument does not provide a finite-order observed rational inverse for this overlapping two-cycle motif. Ribot–Seigal–Zwiernik's unrestricted-mixing obstruction does not settle recovery of only (a,d) after imposing the SEM zero pattern. Jiang's eigenvector construction requires a diagonal higher-order source cumulant, whereas eps2 can carry uncontrolled mixed third cumulants with both endpoints. The missing step is therefore query-specific elimination of nuisance cumulants and central coefficients through coupled residual equations.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit observable chart D and proof that D nonzero makes the complex zero set of the three residual cross-cumulants exactly {(a,d)}, together with a rational inverse obtained from the linear first subresultant of the resulting observable cubics.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing covariance results establish cyclic noninjectivity but do not construct a local fiber whose disturbance laws remain legal here or prove that its projection moves (a,d). Prior CausalSmith work warns that failure of a rank certificate is not an information lower bound and that complex algebraic overlap does not automatically produce real moment-feasible twins. The required lower bound must therefore realize a positive-definite covariance neighborhood with independent non-Gaussian endpoints along a smooth query-moving curve. Conversely, the order-three argument must establish singleton recovery and classify the real fibers on D=0 rather than merely exhibit a sufficient generic chart.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The nearest cumulant estimators give pointwise smooth-map or minimum-distance limits for full mixing models. Here the moment vector contains parameter-dependent residuals and plug-in centered third cumulants, while its optimal weight estimates their influence covariance from the same sample. Uniformity requires simultaneous control of sample centering, sixth-order envelopes, weight inversion, global separation from false roots, and lower singular-value margins for the residual Jacobian and influence covariance. The prior CausalSmith entries independently identify uniform cumulant expansions, estimated transformations, and weak denominators as unresolved proof boundaries; none supplies the required uniform Z-estimator argument on the stated Wasserstein class.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A feasible two-step GMM estimator with an explicit centered-third-cumulant influence function and a uniform expansion sqrt(n)((ahat,dhat)-(a,d))=n^(-1/2) sum_i psi_P(X_i)+o_P(1), uniformly consistent optimal-weight and sandwich-covariance estimators, and a uniformly covering chi-square ellipse with observable margin diagnostics.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Full-distribution cyclic work establishes that observational equivalence can persist, but does not distinguish a point-identified outer projection from the central nuisance fiber in this disturbance model. The banked cyclic-effect construction uses independent latent source directions and a latent-row shear, assumptions unavailable when eps2 may depend arbitrarily on both endpoints. Its completion argument must be replaced by a distribution-preserving residual shear that changes (b,c) while preserving endpoint independence, connected-set Markov legality, invertibility, and the entire observed law; a converse is then needed to exclude additional compatible central parameterizations.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit two-parameter residual-shear action preserving the observed law and every disturbance restriction, together with a converse theorem proving that its orbit is the full compatible (b,c) fiber while the projection onto (a,d) is a singleton.

open_problems.why_unsolved: A positive lower bound on D and the residual Jacobian supports ordinary uniform Wald inference but excludes near-singular sequences. Here weakness is nonlinear: the two observable cubics approach a nontransverse common root, and the rational inverse divides by a vanishing first-subresultant coefficient. Existing weak-GMM and subvector-IV procedures do not directly cover polynomial residual-cumulant moments with estimated third-cumulant covariance. A valid construction must derive the appropriate local experiment or invert a statistic without dividing by the weak chart factor.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An identification-robust test inversion or quasi-Bayes confidence set for (a,d) with uniform coverage over local sequences D_n tending to zero or sigma_min(J_n) tending to zero, plus a theorem characterizing boundedness and convergence to the strong-chart sandwich ellipse.

writing_exemplar.why: Its proposed link between wide confidence intervals and failed genericity supplies the natural motivation for chart-aware weak-identification inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Generic identification holds away from an algebraic exceptional set -> data may lie near that set -> Wald intervals become unstable and diagnostically wide -> invert residual moments without dividing by the weak chart

method_exemplars.technique: Replace discontinuous GMM argmin behavior under weak identification with continuous bagged or quasi-Bayes rules derived from a weak-GMM limit experiment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A vanishing subresultant coefficient creates the moment-map discontinuity their framework targets, although the cyclic-cumulant local experiment remains to be derived.

method_exemplars.technique: Profile nuisance parameters in a score statistic, invert the subvector test, and connect confidence-set boundedness to rejection of rank deficiency.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is only the two-dimensional outer-coefficient subvector, and boundedness should analogously be tied to an observable rank or subresultant diagnostic.

literature_map:
1. Drton–Foygel–Sullivant (2011, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1003.1146) characterize covariance identification in linear SEMs and show that cyclic covariance maps can be noninjective.
2. Foygel–Draisma–Drton (2012, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1107.5552) give half-trek generic-identification criteria allowing cycles, but remain second-order and graph-wide.
3. Draisma–Kuhnt–Zwiernik (2013, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1207.5910) study transformation groups and equivariant inference for Gaussian graphical models; this is not a non-Gaussian cyclic-SEM cumulant-identification result.
4. Lacerda–Spirtes–Ramsey–Hoyer (2008, UAI, arXiv:1206.3273) extend ICA-based LiNG discovery to cycles under mutually independent errors and generally recover an equivalence class rather than a unique SEM.
5. Hyvarinen–Smith (2013, JMLR) develop residual and likelihood-ratio LiNGAM scores and heuristically reuse them for cyclic models while retaining independent disturbances.
6. Wang–Drton (2017, Stat, arXiv:1710.02588) provide empirical-likelihood inference for mixed-graph SEMs with dependent errors, but not a cyclic query-specific third-cumulant inverse.
7. Wang–Drton (2023, JMLR, arXiv:2007.11131) recover bow-free acyclic causal structure from non-Gaussian dependent-error moments; directed feedback is excluded.
8. Mesters–Zwiernik (2024, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2206.13668) identify full mixing matrices from structured cumulant zeros and give pointwise minimum-distance inference, usually with stronger global source restrictions.
9. Tramontano–Drton–Etesami (2026, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2405.20856) give a complete acyclic direct-effect criterion under connected-set Markov errors, partial cyclic results, and leave complete cyclic characterization, weaker moment assumptions, and confidence intervals open.
10. Jiang (2025, arXiv:2501.06777) removes covariance whitening when a higher-order source cumulant is diagonal and derives a root-n estimator; arbitrary middle-error cross-cumulants remain outside its assumptions.
11. Ribot–Seigal–Zwiernik (2025, arXiv:2510.07525) prove full component recovery under pairwise mean independence and generic full-mixing nonidentification once one such condition is dropped, leaving graph- and query-specific recovery below that threshold unresolved.
12. Ribot–Seigal–Zwiernik (2025, arXiv:2506.19009) prove generic uniqueness of orthogonal tensor eigenbases, supplying tensor geometry for full component models rather than a sparse cyclic residual inverse.
13. Mesters–Ribot–Seigal–Zwiernik (2026, arXiv:2605.04381) use sequential residual tests for acyclic discovery under mean-independent dependent noises; their source-node recursion does not address feedback.
14. Hansen (1982, Econometrica) supplies optimal GMM and sandwich theory, while Andrews–Mikusheva (2022, arXiv:2204.12462) and Londschien–Buhlmann (2026, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2407.15256) motivate separate inference near rank or chart singularities.
15. No located paper gives a query-specific order-three rational inverse for this overlapping-cycle/path-dependent motif, a sharp order-two versus order-three fiber theorem for (a,d), or uniform sixth-moment sandwich inference with observable chart margins.
